law.statement: A tool binary activates only when its archive sha256, source URL and per-target pin all match; a revoked or re-cut pin at the same version refuses; identity write failure rolls back activation.
law.oracle_witness: packages/core/src/ripgrep/acquire.ts with packages/core/test/ripgrep-acquire.test.ts at oracle 42e4888cc0 (19/0, mutation-proven), consumed as observable compatibility evidence only

typed_values.name: ToolName
typed_values.shape: 1..=64 [a-z0-9._-], leading byte [a-z0-9], no Windows reserved device name
typed_values.law: names the tool: the first layout segment of the activation tree; a segment the host treats as a device is not a name, and the identity record and pin must agree on it

typed_values.name: ToolVersion
typed_values.law: upstream release version; equal version with a changed digest is a re-cut, not an upgrade

typed_values.name: TargetTriple
typed_values.law: the per-target pin key; an absent entry is target-unsupported, never a default

typed_values.name: SourceUrl
typed_values.shape: 1..=1024 bytes, no control bytes, scheme-less relative path
typed_values.law: the exact position of the archive relative to the activation root; the shipped deterministic adapter admits scheme-less relative paths only, so any scheme prefix (including file:) is refused source-unsupported (R11), and a network source is an explicit release-input boundary, not a core capability

typed_values.name: Sha256
typed_values.law: archive digest and binary digest are separate facts and both are carried in the identity

typed_values.name: ArchiveFormat
typed_values.law: the shipped bounded decoder admits only uncompressed ustar tar; the vocabulary is a closed typed value, so a pin declaring any other format is refused pin-malformed (R06) at pin decode — a runtime format refusal is unreachable, which is why revision 2 removed R12 from the matrix

typed_values.name: EntryName
typed_values.shape: 1..=256 bytes, relative, no dot segments, no absolute, final segment not a Windows reserved device name
typed_values.law: the pinned path of the binary inside the archive; the final segment is where the executable lands on disk

typed_values.name: InstalledIdentity
typed_values.law: presence of a binary is not evidence of provenance; only a record that matches the CURRENT pin vouches for it

match_law: identity matches the current pin only when tool, version, platform, arch, target, source AND archive_sha256 all equal, and the canonical bytes hash to identity.binary_sha256; version and target alone never match, so a revoked or re-cut pin at the same version refuses reuse and re-acquires

refusal_matrix.condition: the activation root does not exist or is not a directory
the root exists but the tool directory tree cannot be read or created
the pin file does not exist
the pin file exists but cannot be read or is not a regular file
the pin file exceeds the 64 KiB bound
the pin file is not a JSON object, carries a foreign schema, or a typed field is absent or out of bound
the pin file's directory is not a Git worktree, or the git attribution plumbing cannot be believed; an unattributable pin is a non-Git workspace state, not missing data
the pin file sits in a worktree but is not tracked at HEAD
the pin file is tracked but its on-disk bytes differ from the HEAD blob; an uncommitted re-cut is not an admissible pin, the pin change is a commit
the well-formed pin table has no entry for the requested target

the pin names a source the shipped deterministic adapter does not admit: it delivers scheme-less relative paths under the activation root only, so any scheme prefix (including file:) or a non-relative location refuses; a network source is an explicit release-input boundary, not a core capability
the deterministic adapter could not deliver the pinned archive bytes
the delivered archive bytes do not hash to the pinned archive sha256; nothing is staged or activated
the verified archive does not contain the pinned entry
a symlink, hardlink, absolute path, dot segment, non-regular entry, or a bound violation (entry count, path depth, entry size, name length) inside the archive

the tar stream is structurally inconsistent at the framing level: an empty stream, not a whole number of blocks, a single zero block, data after the terminator, an entry size overrun, non-zero padding, or a missing terminator
another activation holds the exclusive lock; concurrent callers serialize rather than race, and no partial bytes are exposed
the staged executable re-reads to a digest different from the verified binary digest; the staged file is removed and the previous activation is untouched
the staged-to-canonical rename failed; the canonical path is untouched (the previous executable remains when there was one) and the staged file is removed

the identity record cannot be written after the binary is in place; activation rolls back: the new binary is removed, the previous executable and its record restored (or nothing left when there was no previous), so an unattributable binary is never left executable

a header or entry the decoder cannot verify or parse: over the byte bound, a non-NUL-terminated name, non-octal size or checksum fields, an unverified header checksum, non-ustar magic, a foreign ustar version, a prefix without a name, or a directory entry with non-zero size

diagnostic_law: every refusal that has a decoded pin entry names the failed tool, version, target, source and pin archive digest; earlier refusals name the facts they have; no diagnostic leaks filesystem paths or secrets

base_counterexample.expected_at_base: the product binary has no toolchain verb (unknown-command refusal, exit 2) and the workspace has no grapt-toolchain member: S1 has no Rust owner at the accepted base
base_counterexample.proves: S1 is not already satisfied: no typed activation contract, no verified staged activation, no re-cut refusal, no identity-write rollback anywhere in the Rust product

revisions.1: J01 witness matrix, as first authored from the code's refusal taxonomy.
revisions.2: Two amendments, both aligning the matrix to behavior the code already proved: (a) R12 (format-unsupported) removed — the format vocabulary is a closed typed value, so a foreign format string is a malformed pin refused R06 at pin decode; the runtime reason was unreachable, and an unreachable row is not a refusal the boundary owes. The matrix now carries twenty reasons, R01..R21 minus R12, which is the set the code's taxonomy test counts. (b) SourceUrl corrected — the shipped deterministic adapter admits scheme-less relative paths only; any scheme prefix, including file:, is refused source-unsupported (R11). Revision 1's 'file: scheme only' wording described an adapter the code never shipped.
revisions.3: Review corrections on the composed candidate: (a) R22 (archive-malformed) added and R17 reframed to framing facts only — a header the decoder cannot verify or parse is malformed, a short or cut stream is truncation; the matrix now carries twenty-one reasons, R01..R22 minus R12. (b) The binary bound unified into the single 8 MiB archive bound: the archive decodes in memory and is never staged as a file, so a separate binary staging bound was a second owner of one fact. (c) The publish law restated: the previous executable is retained as a hard link to last-known-good, then ONE replace-existing rename publishes; a crash anywhere in the window leaves the previous or the new executable at the canonical path, never neither (R20 reframed to match). (d) ToolName and EntryName gain the layout-segment law: the first and final segments of the activation tree must not be names a host filesystem treats as devices. (e) The diagnostic context gains the pin source and archive digest for every refusal after pin decode. (f) The product seam admits a target only when it describes this host: the seam activates the host's own tool tree.
